assignedReviews.card_evidence: The batteries we use in flashlights and watches are dry cells, which contain an electrolyte in a paste form instead of a liquid.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the construction of dry cells (batteries), which is an electricity topic. It provides no information about gravity as a non-contact force or its predictable effects on objects.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The batteries we use in flashlights and watches are dry cells, which contain an electrolyte in a paste form instead of a liquid.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about dry cells and electrolytes, not about observing or describing the effects of gravity on the motion of an object. No gravity content is present.

copy.en: The batteries we use in flashlights and watches are dry cells, which contain an electrolyte in a paste form instead of a liquid.
copy.tl: Ang mga battery na ginagamit natin sa flashlights at watches ay dry cells, na naglalaman ng electrolyte sa anyong paste sa halip na liquid.
copy.bis: Ang mga battery nga atong gigamit sa flashlights ug watches kay dry cells, nga adunay electrolyte sa porma nga paste imbes nga liquid.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: let the slide dry so it can be stained
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a microscope slide preparation technique (drying a smear before staining or covering). It does not address chemical properties of materials such as burning, reactivity, or biodegradability, which are the focus of G4-M-3.

copy.en: After making a smear, you can either let the slide dry so it can be stained, or place a coverslip on top of the smear right away.
copy.tl: Pagkatapos gumawa ng smear, maaari mong hayaang matuyo ang slide para ito ay ma-stain, o lagyan agad ng coverslip ang ibabaw ng smear.
copy.bis: Human maghimo ug smear, mahimo nimo nga paugaon ang slide aron kini ma-stain, o butangan dayon ug coverslip ang ibabaw sa smear.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sunlight helps dry clothes quickly
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that chemical equations demonstrate a rearrangement of atoms but the total mass of the system remains the same during a chemical reaction
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes evaporation of water from clothes due to sunlight, a physical change. It does not address chemical equations, rearrangement of atoms, or conservation of mass in chemical reactions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sunlight helps dry clothes quickly
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: apply the principles of conservation of mass to balance chemical equations
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about drying clothes, not about balancing chemical equations or applying conservation of mass. No chemical reaction is involved.

copy.en: Sunlight helps dry clothes quickly, so people hang wet clothes outside on sunny days.
copy.tl: Nakakatulong ang sunlight para mabilis na matuyo ang mga damit, kaya isinasampay ng mga tao ang basang damit sa labas kapag maaraw.
copy.bis: Ang kahayag sa Adlaw makatabang nga dali mamala ang mga sanina, mao nga isab-ay sa mga tao ang basang sanina sa gawas kon adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When rice is harvested, farmers spread the grains in a thin layer under the Sun
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw the structure of an atom in terms of the nucleus and electron shells
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes sun-drying of rice grains; it contains no information about the structure of an atom, nucleus, or electron shells.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When rice is harvested, farmers spread the grains in a thin layer under the Sun
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: develop a timeline for the historical background of the development of the current Atomic Model that identifies tiny particles as atoms
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about agricultural drying practice and provides no historical background or timeline for the development of the atomic model.

copy.en: When rice is harvested, farmers spread the grains in a thin layer under the Sun and turn them every 30 to 60 minutes so they dry evenly.
copy.tl: Kapag inani na ang palay, ikinakalat ng mga magsasaka ang mga butil sa manipis na layer sa ilalim ng Araw at binabaligtad ito tuwing 30 hanggang 60 minuto para matuyo nang pantay.
copy.bis: Kon anihon na ang humay, ibuklad sa mga mag-uuma ang mga lugas sa nipis nga layer ilalom sa Adlaw ug balihon kini matag 30 hangtod 60 ka minuto aron mamala nga patas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ductile materials can be stretched into wires without breaking
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some effects of weather disturbances that occur in or near the Philippines
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the physical property of ductility in metals (gold, silver, copper). It has no connection to weather disturbances in or near the Philippines.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ductile materials can be stretched into wires without breaking
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about material properties, not about weather conditions before, during, or after a tropical cyclone.

copy.en: Ductile materials can be stretched into wires without breaking, such as gold, silver, and copper.
copy.tl: Ang mga ductile na materyales ay maaaring hatakin para maging wire nang hindi napuputol, tulad ng ginto, pilak, at tanso.
copy.bis: Ang mga ductile nga materyales mahimong inaton aron mahimong wire nga dili maputol, sama sa bulawan, pilak, ug tumbaga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: There are many varieties of durian, and they differ in taste, flesh color, and smell.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that durian varieties differ in taste, color, and smell. It does not use a table, classify living things into the named groups (flowering/non-flowering plants, animal groups, microorganisms), or present any classification scheme. The competency requires a table-based classification, which is entirely absent.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: There are many varieties of durian, and they differ in taste, flesh color, and smell.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses variation among durian varieties, not the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It provides no information about growth, response, or reproduction, so it does not support this competency.

copy.en:
Do all durians taste the same?

No! There are many varieties of durian, and they differ in taste, flesh color, and smell.
copy.tl:
Magkakapareho ba ang lasa ng lahat ng durian?

Hindi pala! May iba't ibang uri ng durian, at nagkakaiba sila sa lasa, kulay ng laman, at amoy.
copy.bis:
Managsama ba tanang durian og lami?

Dili diay! Adunay lainlaing klase sa durian, ug managlahi sila sa lami, kolor sa unod, ug baho.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your ear canal is a tube leading from the outer ear to the eardrum.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The competency targets outer body parts of animals (head, legs, wings) and their roles in movement and food gathering. The card describes the human ear canal, an internal structure, and its protective function via earwax, which does not align with the competency's subject or action.

copy.en: Your ear canal is a tube leading from the outer ear to the eardrum. It makes earwax, which protects your eardrum from dust and tiny insects.
copy.tl: Ang ear canal ay tubo mula sa panlabas na tenga papunta sa eardrum. Gumagawa ito ng earwax na nagpoprotekta sa eardrum mula sa alikabok at maliliit na insekto.
copy.bis: Ang ear canal usa ka tubo gikan sa gawas nga tenga paingon sa eardrum. Naghimo kini og earwax nga nanalipod sa eardrum gikan sa abog ug gagmayng insekto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the fluid inside our ears keeps moving even after we stop
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains dizziness from spinning due to inner ear fluid, but G4-L-1 requires describing the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems. The ear/balance system is not among these, so the card does not support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the fluid inside our ears keeps moving even after we stop
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: G3-L-3 is about characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). The card discusses a sensory/balance response in humans, not growth, response in the sense of the competency, or reproduction. It is unrelated to the stated characteristics.

copy.en:
Why do we feel dizzy after spinning?

When we spin fast, the fluid inside our ears keeps moving even after we stop — that's what makes us feel dizzy!
copy.tl:
Bakit tayo nahihilo pagkatapos umikot?

Kapag mabilis tayong umiikot, patuloy pang gumagalaw ang likido sa loob ng tainga kahit tumigil na tayo — kaya tayo nahihilo!
copy.bis:
Ngano molipong ta human motuyok?

Kon kusog kitang motuyok, ang likido sa sulod sa dalunggan magpadayon paglihok bisan mihunong na kita — mao nga molipong kita!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Our ears catch sound waves and then send signals to the brain
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe the possible effects of human activities, such as deforestation, pollution, and introduction of invasive species, on living things in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the ear and brain processing sound waves. It has no connection to human activities (deforestation, pollution, invasive species) affecting ecosystems, which is the subject of G9-L-10.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Our ears catch sound waves and then send signals to the brain
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about hearing and the brain, not about the root and shoot system of plants. It does not support observing or describing plant root/shoot systems.

copy.en: Our ears catch sound waves and then send signals to the brain, which understands them as sounds.
copy.tl: Sinasalo ng ating mga tenga ang sound waves at nagpapadala ito ng signals sa utak, na siyang umuunawa sa mga tunog.
copy.bis: Ang atong mga dalunggan mosalo sa sound waves ug dayon magpadala og signals ngadto sa utok, nga maoy makasabot sa mga tingog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth is called the Blue Planet because of its abundant liquid water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes Earth's water and distance from the Sun; it contains no information about plant outer parts (leaves, roots, stems) or their role in water/nutrient uptake.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth is called the Blue Planet because of its abundant liquid water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how plant organs (leaf, stem, roots) work together as the transport system
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not discuss plant organs or the transport system; it is about Earth's water and distance from the Sun, unrelated to plant organ function.

copy.en: Earth is called the Blue Planet because of its abundant liquid water, and it is about 149 million kilometers from the Sun.
copy.tl: Ang Earth ay tinatawag na Blue Planet dahil sa masaganang likidong tubig nito, at ito ay mga 149 million kilometers mula sa Araw.
copy.bis: Ang Earth gitawag nga Blue Planet tungod sa daghang likidong tubig niini, ug kini mga 149 million kilometers gikan sa Adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth's magnetic field acts like a giant shield!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to identify the properties of magnets, including how they affect other magnets and objects made of different materials
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about investigating the properties of magnets and how they affect other magnets and objects made of different materials. The card describes Earth's magnetic field as a shield against solar particles, which is a different concept (planetary magnetism and space weather) and does not support the guided investigation of magnet properties or interactions with objects.

copy.en: Earth's magnetic field acts like a giant shield! It blocks harmful particles coming straight from the Sun.
copy.tl: Ang magnetic field ng Daigdig ay parang panangga! Pinipigilan nito ang mapaminsalang particle mula sa Araw.
copy.bis: Ang magnetic field sa Kalibutan sama sa taming! Nagpugong kini sa makadaot nga mga tipik gikan sa Adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Examples of earth materials include rocks, soil, sand, water, minerals, and fossil fuels.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how plant organs (leaf, stem, roots) work together as the transport system
assignedReviews.reason: The card lists earth materials (rocks, soil, sand, water, minerals, fossil fuels) and says nothing about plant organs (leaf, stem, roots) or their transport system. No instructional support for G8-L-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Examples of earth materials include rocks, soil, sand, water, minerals, and fossil fuels.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about non-living earth materials, not the outer parts of plants (leaves, roots, stems) or their role in getting water and nutrients. No instructional support for G3-L-5.

copy.en: Examples of earth materials include rocks, soil, sand, water, minerals, and fossil fuels.
copy.tl: Ang mga halimbawa ng earth materials ay rocks, soil, sand, water, minerals, at fossil fuels.
copy.bis: Ang mga pananglitan sa earth materials mao ang rocks, soil, sand, water, minerals, ug fossil fuels.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The atmosphere is the layer of gases surrounding Earth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how high voltage electricity from power plants is generated and safely distributed to industries, businesses, and homes, including the role of substations (grid stations), and electric meters
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the atmosphere and its gases, which is unrelated to the competency about high voltage electricity generation and distribution from power plants, substations, and electric meters.

copy.en: The atmosphere is the layer of gases surrounding Earth, providing oxygen for animals and carbon dioxide for plants.
copy.tl: Ang atmosphere ay ang layer ng mga gas na nakapalibot sa Earth, na nagbibigay ng oxygen para sa mga hayop at carbon dioxide para sa mga halaman.
copy.bis: Ang atmosphere mao ang layer sa mga gas nga naglibot sa Earth, nga naghatag ug oxygen para sa mga mananap ug carbon dioxide para sa mga tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Precession is the slow wobble of Earth's axis
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in solid materials make them useful, such as when they are shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, or cut
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes Earth's axial precession and its effect on seasons over thousands of years. This is an Earth science concept, not a change in solid materials making them useful. No support for G3-M-8.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Precession is the slow wobble of Earth's axis
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: determine how forces can change the shape of objects such as when they are pushed, pulled, stretched, bent, twisted, or squeezed
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses Earth's wobble (precession) and seasonal timing, not forces changing the shape of objects. No support for G4-F-6.

copy.en: Precession is the slow wobble of Earth's axis, like a spinning top, which changes the timing of seasons over thousands of years.
copy.tl: Ang precession ay ang mabagal na pag-uga ng axis ng Earth, tulad ng isang spinning top, na nagbabago sa timing ng mga panahon sa loob ng libu-libong taon.
copy.bis: Ang precession mao ang hinay nga pag-uyog sa axis sa Earth, sama sa usa ka spinning top, nga nag-usab sa timing sa mga panahon sa liboan ka mga tuig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earthquakes can be weak or strong
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate through guided investigation the advantages and limitations of simple machines, such as inclined planes, wedges, levers, and pulleys
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes earthquake intensity and destruction, which is unrelated to simple machines (inclined planes, wedges, levers, pulleys) or their advantages/limitations.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earthquakes can be weak or strong
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe examples and uses of simple machines found at home, at school, and in the community
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about earthquake effects, not about observing or describing examples and uses of simple machines at home, school, or community.

copy.en: Earthquakes can be weak or strong, and the shaking they cause can bring destruction to buildings, roads, and communities near the fault.
copy.tl: Ang mga lindol ay maaaring mahina o malakas, at ang pagyanig nito ay maaaring magdulot ng pinsala sa mga gusali, kalsada, at komunidad malapit sa fault.
copy.bis: Ang mga linog mahimong huyang o kusog, ug ang pag-uyog nga gipahinabo niini makadala og kadaot sa mga bilding, dalan, ug komunidad duol sa fault.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The magnitude of an earthquake depends on the energy contained in each seismic wave
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses earthquake magnitude, seismic wave energy, and distance from the epicenter. It does not address landforms, bodies of water, or their influence on living and non-living components, so it does not support G5-E-1.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The magnitude of an earthquake depends on the energy contained in each seismic wave
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about earthquake magnitude and epicenter distance, not weather characteristics such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, humidity, rain, or cloud cover. It does not support G4-E-4.

copy.en: The magnitude of an earthquake depends on the energy contained in each seismic wave, and its strength depends on how near or far a person is from the epicenter.
copy.tl: Ang magnitude ng lindol ay nakadepende sa energy na taglay ng bawat seismic wave, at ang lakas nito ay nakadepende kung gaano kalapit o kalayo ang isang tao mula sa epicenter.
copy.bis: Ang magnitude sa linog nagdepende sa energy nga dala sa matag seismic wave, ug ang kusog niini nagdepende kung unsa ka duol o kalayo ang usa ka tawo sa epicenter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: stop the car in a clear space away from buildings and trees
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about earthquake safety while driving; it does not address local landforms/water bodies or their influence on environmental components.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: stop the car in a clear space away from buildings and trees
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify what proportion of the Earth's surface is covered with water as opposed to land
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about earthquake safety while driving; it does not address the proportion of Earth's surface covered by water versus land.

copy.en: If you are driving when an earthquake happens, stop the car in a clear space away from buildings and trees, and remain inside the car until the shaking stops.
copy.tl: Kung ikaw ay nagmamaneho habang lumilindol, ihinto ang sasakyan sa isang malinaw na lugar na malayo sa mga gusali at puno, at manatili sa loob ng sasakyan hanggang sa tumigil ang pagyanig.
copy.bis: Kung ikaw nagdrayb samtang naglinog, ihunong ang sakyanan sa usa ka hawan nga lugar nga layo sa mga bilding ug kahoy, ug pabilin sa sulud sa sakyanan hangtod mohunong ang pagkurog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Transform boundaries can create deep, shallow earthquakes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses transform boundaries and earthquakes at mid-ocean ridges, which is a geology/earth science topic. G3-M-9 requires identifying properties and uses of metals such as iron, gold, silver, and copper. There is no connection to metals or their properties/uses.

copy.en: Transform boundaries can create deep, shallow earthquakes, which are common at mid-ocean ridges but usually do not produce deadly tsunamis.
copy.tl: Ang transform boundaries ay maaaring lumikha ng malalalim at mababaw na lindol, na karaniwan sa mid-ocean ridges ngunit hindi karaniwang nagdudulot ng nakamamatay na tsunami.
copy.bis: Ang transform boundaries makamugna og lawom ug mabaw nga mga linog, nga kasagarang mahitabo sa mid-ocean ridges apan dili kasagarang makapahinabo og makamatay nga tsunami.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Modeling clay and dough are easily pressed
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary resources to classify animals and plants of the Philippines as critically endangered, endangered, or vulnerable species
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the physical property of modeling clay and dough being soft and easily pressed into shapes. This has no connection to classifying Philippine animals and plants as critically endangered, endangered, or vulnerable species.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Modeling clay and dough are easily pressed
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss as a class how threats to biodiversity can lead to species extinction
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the malleability of modeling clay and dough, not about threats to biodiversity or species extinction. It does not support any part of the competency.

copy.en: Modeling clay and dough are easily pressed because they are soft and can be squashed into new shapes with your hands.
copy.tl: Ang modeling clay at dough ay madaling mapisil dahil malambot ang mga ito at kayang mapisil sa mga bagong hugis gamit ang iyong mga kamay.
copy.bis: Ang modeling clay ug dough dali ra mapisil tungod kay humok kini ug mahimo nga mapisil ngadto sa bag-ong mga porma gamit ang imong mga kamot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Healthy foods give your body the nutrients it needs to keep your heart strong and your lungs working well!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how plant organs (leaf, stem, roots) work together as the transport system
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about human nutrition and the heart and lungs. It does not address plant organs (leaf, stem, roots) or their transport system.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Healthy foods give your body the nutrients it needs to keep your heart strong and your lungs working well!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses human health and organs, not the outer parts of plants (leaves, roots, stems) or their role in getting water and nutrients from soil.

copy.en:
Why should I eat the right kind of food?

Healthy foods give your body the nutrients it needs to keep your heart strong and your lungs working well!
copy.tl:
Bakit kailangan kong kumain ng tamang pagkain?

Ang masustansyang pagkain ay nagbibigay ng nutrients na kailangan para manatiling malakas ang puso at maayos ang paggana ng baga!
copy.bis:
Ngano kinahanglan mokaon ko ug husto nga pagkaon?

Ang masustansyang pagkaon naghatag sa imong lawas sa mga nutrients nga gikinahanglan aron magpabiling lig-on ang kasingkasing ug maayo ang pagtrabaho sa baga!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Biotic factors like pests and abiotic factors like sunlight and rain work together to shape how every plant grows.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses ecosystem dynamics and biotic/abiotic factors affecting plant growth. It contains no information about the solar system, celestial objects, or their structure/composition.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Biotic factors like pests and abiotic factors like sunlight and rain work together to shape how every plant grows.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about ecosystem changes and plant growth, not about observing or describing natural objects in the sky such as the Sun, Moon, planets, or stars.

copy.en:
Why do some plants in the garden look different after a few weeks?

Because the ecosystem is always changing! Biotic factors like pests and abiotic factors like sunlight and rain work together to shape how every plant grows.
copy.tl:
Bakit nagkakaiba ang itsura ng ilang halaman sa hardin pagkalipas ng ilang linggo?

Dahil ang ecosystem ay laging nagbabago! Ang mga biotic factors gaya ng pests at abiotic factors gaya ng sikat ng araw at ulan ay nagtutulungan upang hubugin kung paano tumutubo ang bawat halaman.
copy.bis:
Ngano lainlain ang dagway sa pipila ka tanom sa tanaman human sa pipila ka semana?

Tungod kay ang ecosystem kanunay nga nagbag-o! Ang mga biotic factors sama sa pests ug abiotic factors sama sa kahayag sa adlaw ug ulan magtinabangay aron mahulma kung giunsa pagtubo ang matag tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Climate change can cause stronger typhoons
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes effects of climate change (stronger typhoons, droughts, rising sea levels, habitat loss). G3-E-6 requires guided activities to observe and describe natural objects in the sky (Sun, Moon, planets, stars). The card provides no information about celestial objects and does not support this competency.

copy.en: Climate change can cause stronger typhoons, longer droughts, rising sea levels, and the loss of homes for many plants and animals.
copy.tl: Ang climate change ay maaaring magdulot ng mas malalakas na bagyo, mas mahabang tagtuyot, pagtaas ng lebel ng dagat, at pagkawala ng tirahan ng maraming halaman at hayop.
copy.bis: Ang climate change mahimong magpahinabo sa mas kusog nga mga bagyo, mas taas nga hulaw, pagsaka sa lebel sa dagat, ug pagkawala sa puy-anan sa daghang tanom ug mananap.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Around day 14 of a 28-day cycle, ovulation happens.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that scientists use models to explain phenomena that cannot be easily seen or detected
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the timing of ovulation in the menstrual cycle. It does not mention models, scientists, or the use of models to explain unobservable phenomena, which is the core of G7-M-1. The content is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en:
When does the egg come out?

Around day 14 of a 28-day cycle, ovulation happens. One ovary releases a mature egg, ready to meet a sperm.
copy.tl:
Kailan lumalabas ang itlog?

Sa ika-14 na araw ng 28-day cycle, nangyayari ang ovulation. Naglalabas ang isang ovary ng mature egg na handa nang makipagtagpo sa sperm.
copy.bis:
Kanus-a mogawas ang itlog?

Sa ika-14 nga adlaw sa 28-day cycle, mahitabo ang ovulation. Ang usa ka ovary magpagawas ug hamtong nga itlog nga andam na nga makigtagbo sa sperm.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: What is the first stage in the life cycle of animals and plants?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the first stage of life cycles (egg for animals, seed for plants). It provides no information about particle motion, spacing, attraction, or temperature effects, which are the focus of G7-M-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: What is the first stage in the life cycle of animals and plants?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses life cycles, not electric current, voltage, resistance, or series/parallel circuits. It does not support any part of G9-F-7.

copy.en:
What is the first stage in the life cycle of animals and plants?

Animals begin as an egg, while plants begin as a seed!
copy.tl:
Ano ang unang yugto sa life cycle ng mga hayop at halaman?

Ang mga hayop ay nagsisimula bilang itlog, habang ang mga halaman ay nagsisimula bilang buto!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang unang yugto sa life cycle sa mga mananap ug tanom?

Ang mga mananap magsugod isip itlog, samtang ang mga tanom magsugod isip liso!

assignedReviews.reason: The card is about electrical symbols, not about balancing chemical equations or conservation of mass. It provides no support for G10-M-7.

copy.tl: Ang mga common electrical symbols ay mga simpleng drawing na kumakatawan sa mga components tulad ng switch, cell, battery, wires, at bulb sa isang circuit diagram.
copy.bis: Ang mga common electrical symbols kay simple nga mga drawing nga nagrepresentar sa mga components sama sa switch, cell, battery, wires, ug bulb sa usa ka circuit diagram.

copy.bis: Samtang nag-agos ang electric current, ang electromagnet mobira sa mga magnetic nga butang sama sa lansang ug paper clips.

copy.bis: Ang electron affinity, ang pagbag-o sa energy kung ang usa ka atom modawat og electron, nagpakita og periodic trends sa mga period ug group.

copy.en: Robert Millikan was the first to determine the charge of the electron.
copy.tl: Si Robert Millikan ang unang nakatukoy sa charge ng electron.
copy.bis: Si Robert Millikan ang unang nakatino sa charge sa electron.

assignedReviews.reason: The card states the elemental composition of carbohydrates, which is a chemistry/biochemistry fact. It provides no information about typhoon development or why the Philippines is prone to typhoons.

copy.bis: Ang carbohydrates adunay carbon, hydrogen, ug oxygen.

copy.en: At first, the growing life inside is called an embryo. As it develops further, it becomes what we call a fetus.
copy.tl: Sa simula, ang umuusbong na buhay ay tinatawag na embryo. Habang lumalaki ito, ito ay nagiging fetus.
copy.bis: Sa sinugdan, ang nagtubo nga kinabuhi gitawag og embryo. Samtang motubo kini, mahimo kining fetus.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Endangered means a species has a very high risk of extinction in the wild

copy.en: Endangered species have very low populations and may become extinct if they are not protected.
copy.tl: Ang endangered species ay may napakababang bilang ng population at maaaring tuluyang mawala kung hindi sila mapoprotektahan.
copy.bis: Ang endangered species adunay hilabihan ka ubos nga gidaghanon sa population ug mahimong mawala sa hingpit kon dili sila mapanalipdan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The thyroid needs iodine to make its hormone
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory

G4-L-1 specifically requires describing the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory systems. The endocrine system is not among these, so the card does not support this competency.

copy.en: The thyroid needs iodine to make its hormone -- that's why Philippine law requires iodized salt, to prevent goiter, the neck swelling caused by lack of iodine.
copy.tl: Kailangan ng thyroid ang yodo para makagawa ng hormone nito -- kaya may batas sa Pilipinas na dapat may yodo ang asin, para maiwasan ang goiter, ang pamamaga ng leeg dahil sa kakulangan ng yodo.
copy.bis: Ang thyroid nagkinahanglan og iodine aron makahimo sa hormone niini -- mao nga adunay balaod sa Pilipinas nga kinahanglan adunay iodine ang asin, aron malikayan ang goiter, ang paghubag sa liog tungod sa kakulang sa iodine.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: At ground level, a falling object's potential energy is zero because its height above the ground is zero.

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses gravitational potential energy at ground level, a physics concept. G7-M-8 concerns identifying the roles of solute and solvent in a solution, which is chemistry and unrelated to the card's content.

assignedReviews.reason: The card is about potential energy of a falling object, not about ion formation or ionic bonds. G9-M-5 requires explaining the loss/gain of electrons to form ions, which has no connection to the card's physics content.

copy.en: At ground level, a falling object's potential energy is zero because its height above the ground is zero.
copy.tl: Sa ground level, ang potential energy ng bumabagsak na bagay ay zero dahil ang taas nito mula sa lupa ay zero.
copy.bis: Sa ground level, ang potential energy sa nagkahulog nga butang zero tungod kay ang gihabugon o kataason kini zero.

copy.en: Electromagnetic waves carry energy as they travel through space.
copy.tl: Ang electromagnetic waves ay nagdadala ng energy habang naglalakbay sa kalawakan.
copy.bis: Ang electromagnetic waves nagdala ug energy samtang nagbiyahe sa kawanangan.

copy.en: Environmental conditions such as food, water, temperature, and calamities affect the life cycle of organisms.
copy.tl: Ang mga kondisyon ng kapaligiran tulad ng pagkain, tubig, temperatura, at mga kalamidad ay nakakaapekto sa life cycle ng mga organismo.
copy.bis: Ang mga kondisyon sa kalikopan sama sa pagkaon, tubig, temperatura, ug mga kalamidad makaapekto sa life cycle sa mga organismo.

copy.bis: Ang epididymis usa ka pig-ot ug naglikoliko nga tubo nga magtipig sa mga immature nga sperm cells hangtod sila mohingkod ug andam nang ipagawas.

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses equinoxes and the Sun-Earth geometry, not acids, bases, salts, or indicators. G10-M-2 is a chemistry competency with no connection to the card's content.

copy.en: In March and September, called equinoxes, day and night are nearly equal in length everywhere on Earth because neither pole leans toward the Sun.
copy.tl: Sa Marso at Setyembre, na tinatawag na equinox, halos magkapareho ang haba ng araw at gabi sa lahat ng lugar sa Earth dahil walang pole ang nakahilig patungo sa Araw.
copy.bis: Sa Marso ug Septiyembre, nga gitawag ug equinox, halos parehas ang gitas-on sa adlaw ug gabii sa tanang lugar sa Earth tungod kay walay pole nga nakiling paingon sa Adlaw.

copy.en:
Why is it warm near the equator all year?

The equator always receives sunlight at high angles, so the solar energy stays concentrated and the temperature stays fairly constant.
copy.tl:
Bakit mainit malapit sa equator buong taon?

Laging tumatanggap ang equator ng sikat ng araw sa matataas na anggulo, kaya concentrated ang solar energy at halos hindi nagbabago ang temperatura.
copy.bis:
Ngano init duol sa equator tibuok tuig?

Ang equator kanunay makadawat ug silaw sa adlaw sa taas nga mga anggulo, busa concentrated ang solar energy ug halos dili mausab ang temperatura.

copy.tl: Ang work ay maaari ring sukatin sa ergs, kung saan ang isang joule ay katumbas ng sampung milyong ergs, isang napakaliit na yunit ng work.
copy.bis: Ang work mahimo usab nga sukdon sa ergs, diin ang usa ka joule katumbas sa napulo ka milyon nga ergs, usa ka gamay kaayo nga yunit sa work.

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses erosion removing rock layers, a geological process. G6-E-8 is about a Sun-Earth-Moon system model and seasons/eclipses, which is unrelated to erosion or rock layers.

copy.en: Erosion can remove rock layers from a sequence, leaving a gap where those layers once existed.
copy.tl: Maaaring alisin ng erosion ang mga suson ng bato mula sa isang sequence, na nag-iiwan ng puwang kung saan dating naroon ang mga suson na iyon.
copy.bis: Ang erosion makakuha sa mga sapaw sa bato gikan sa usa ka sequence, nga magbilin ug puwang diin kaniadto nahimutang ang mga sapaw.

copy.bis: Ang exosphere mosagol sa outer space, ug ang gravity sa Earth huyang kaayo didto mao nga ang mga molecule sa gas makalingkawas ngadto sa kawanangan.

copy.tl: Ang estimating ay ang hakbang kung saan sinusukat ng mga manggagawa kung gaano karami ang debris at kinakalkula ang gastos at oras na kailangan para alisin ito.
copy.bis: Ang estimating mao ang lakang diin gisukod sa mga trabahador kung pila ka daghan ang debris ug gikalkula ang gasto ug oras nga gikinahanglan aron makuha kini.

copy.bis: Ang mud flats ug salt marshes mao ang mga habitat nga makita sa estuarine ecosystem, apan ang mango plantation dili.

Ang fingerprint gagmay nga bukol-bukol nga linya sa panit, gitawag friction ridges — tinuod nga bukol, dili pinta nga linya!

copy.bis: Ang husto nga pagdumala sa kalayo naglakip sa pagpalong sa kandila human gamiton, aron dili kini makasugod ug aksidente nga sunog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A first aid kit has gauze, bandages, plasters, antiseptic, and scissors
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the uses of various science equipment and materials used in simple activities, such as a ruler, hand lens, scissors, balloons, modeling clay, and cardboard
assignedReviews.reason: The competency asks students to describe the uses of science equipment and materials used in simple science activities (e.g., ruler, hand lens, scissors, balloons, modeling clay, cardboard). This card only lists the contents of a first aid kit; it does not describe the uses of any science equipment or materials in a science activity context. The mention of scissors is incidental and not tied to a science activity, so the card does not support the competency.

copy.en: A first aid kit has gauze, bandages, plasters, antiseptic, and scissors -- everything you need to treat a small wound.
copy.tl: May laman ang first aid kit na gasa, benda, plaster, antiseptiko, at gunting -- lahat ng kailangan para gamutin ang maliit na sugat.
copy.bis: Adunay sulod ang first aid kit nga gasa, benda, plaster, antiseptiko, ug gunting -- tanan nga kinahanglan sa pag-atiman sa gamay nga samad.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fish bubbles expand as they rise because water pressure decreases near the surface
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains gas expansion due to decreasing water pressure, which is a physics concept unrelated to the solar system, celestial objects, or their composition. It provides no instructional support for G5-E-11.

copy.en: Fish bubbles expand as they rise because water pressure decreases near the surface, letting the gas inside take up more space.
copy.tl: Lumalaki ang bubbles ng isda habang umaakyat ito dahil bumababa ang water pressure malapit sa surface, kaya mas lumalawak ang gas sa loob.
copy.bis: Modako ang bubbles sa isda samtang mosaka kini tungod kay mous-os ang water pressure duol sa surface, busa mas molapad ang gas sa sulod.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The five key threats to biodiversity
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how solar energy contributes to the occurrence of land and sea breezes, monsoons, and the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes threats to biodiversity (habitat loss, overexploitation, pollution, climate change, invasive species). The competency G7-E-12 requires explaining how solar energy contributes to land/sea breezes, monsoons, and the ITCZ. There is no overlap in content; the card does not support this competency at all.

copy.en: The five key threats to biodiversity are habitat loss and degradation, overexploitation, pollution, climate change, and invasive species and disease.
copy.tl: Ang limang pangunahing banta sa biodiversity ay habitat loss at degradation, overexploitation, pollution, climate change, at invasive species at disease.
copy.bis: Ang lima ka pangunang hulga sa biodiversity mao ang habitat loss ug degradation, overexploitation, pollution, climate change, ug invasive species ug disease.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your five sense organs are the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the parts and functions, and demonstrate proper handling and storing of a compound microscope
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the five sense organs and their functions, which is unrelated to identifying parts and functions of a compound microscope or its handling and storing. No microscope content is present.

copy.en: Your five sense organs are the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin, and each one has a special job that helps you understand the world.
copy.tl: Ang limang sense organs mo ay ang mata, tainga, ilong, dila, at balat, at bawat isa ay may sariling trabaho para maintindihan mo ang mundo.
copy.bis: Ang imong lima ka sense organs mao ang mata, dunggan, ilong, dila, ug panit, ug ang matag usa adunay kaugalingong trabaho aron masabtan nimo ang kalibutan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fireworks get their colors because different metallic elements release different amounts of energy as light when their electrons get excited by heat.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: collaborate in a class discussion to recognize the advantages and limitations of using series or parallel circuits
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains flame colors from excited electrons in metallic elements, which is an atomic emission/chemistry topic. G9-F-9 requires recognizing advantages and limitations of series or parallel circuits. There is no connection to circuits, current, voltage, or resistance.

copy.en: Fireworks get their colors because different metallic elements release different amounts of energy as light when their electrons get excited by heat.
copy.tl: Nagkakaroon ng iba't ibang kulay ang fireworks dahil ang iba't ibang metallic elements ay naglalabas ng iba't ibang dami ng energy bilang liwanag kapag na-excite ng init ang kanilang mga electron.
copy.bis: Ang mga fireworks adunay lain-laing kolor tungod kay ang lain-laing metallic elements nagpagawas ug lain-laing gidaghanon sa energy isip kahayag kon ma-excite sa init ang ilang mga electron.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It blocks sodium's bright yellow light so we can clearly see potassium's hidden violet color.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the electron structure of an atom determines its position on the periodic table
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the use of cobalt blue glass to filter sodium's yellow light in flame tests, which is a technique for detecting potassium. It does not address electron structure determining an element's position on the periodic table, nor any related concept such as valence electrons, shells, or periodic trends. The competency is about the relationship between atomic electron configuration and periodic table placement, which the card does not support.

copy.en: COBALT BLUE GLASS is a cool tool in flame tests! It blocks sodium's bright yellow light so we can clearly see potassium's hidden violet color.
copy.tl: Ang COBALT BLUE GLASS ay isang cool na tool sa flame tests! Hinaharang nito ang dilaw na liwanag ng sodium para makita natin ang nakatagong violet na kulay ng potassium.
copy.bis: Ang COBALT BLUE GLASS usa ka cool nga tool sa flame tests! Gibabagan niini ang dalag nga kahayag sa sodium aron makita nato ang nakatago nga violet nga kolor sa potassium.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Covalent compounds with carbon and hydrogen atoms, like LPG, burn easily
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the weather conditions according to a Public Storm Warning Signal issued by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geological and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses flammability of covalent compounds (chemistry), not weather conditions according to PAGASA storm warning signals. No instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Covalent compounds with carbon and hydrogen atoms, like LPG, burn easily
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: examine a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about the local weather and describe and practice safety precautions to use during poor or extreme weather conditions
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about chemical properties of covalent compounds, not about examining local weather charts or safety precautions during poor/extreme weather. Unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Covalent compounds with carbon and hydrogen atoms, like LPG, burn easily because those atoms react with oxygen gas to form carbon dioxide and water.
copy.tl: Ang mga covalent compound na may carbon at hydrogen atoms, tulad ng LPG, ay madaling masunog dahil ang mga atoms na iyon ay tumutugon sa oxygen gas upang bumuo ng carbon dioxide at tubig.
copy.bis: Ang mga covalent compound nga adunay carbon ug hydrogen atoms, sama sa LPG, dali nga masunog tungod kay kana nga mga atoms motubag sa oxygen gas aron moporma ug carbon dioxide ug tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Platyhelminthes, like tapeworms, are flat and elongated invertebrates
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: distinguish among comets, meteoroids, asteroids, and dwarf planets, and describe how they help us to understand the nature and formation of the Earth and the Solar System
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes flatworms (Platyhelminthes), a biology topic. G9-E-9 concerns distinguishing comets, meteoroids, asteroids, and dwarf planets and their role in understanding the Solar System. There is no connection to celestial objects or planetary science.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Platyhelminthes, like tapeworms, are flat and elongated invertebrates
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about flatworm anatomy and habitat, not the structure of the solar system or celestial objects. G5-E-11 requires describing the solar system's major objects and features, which is entirely unrelated to this biology card.

copy.en: Platyhelminthes, like tapeworms, are flat and elongated invertebrates that live in water or inside other animals.
copy.tl: Ang mga platyhelminthes, tulad ng tapeworm, ay mga patag at pahabang invertebrate na nabubuhay sa tubig o sa loob ng ibang mga hayop.
copy.bis: Ang mga platyhelminthes, sama sa tapeworm, mga patag ug taas nga invertebrate nga nagpuyo sa tubig o sa sulud sa laing mga mananap.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Strong flows of water, like floods, can move very large and heavy objects, such as cars and trees.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the force of flood water moving heavy objects, which is unrelated to the competency about describing useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures such as solutions and suspensions.

copy.en: Strong flows of water, like floods, can move very large and heavy objects, such as cars and trees.
copy.tl: Ang malalakas na agos ng tubig, tulad ng baha, ay kayang igalaw ang napakalalaki at mabibigat na bagay, gaya ng mga kotse at puno.
copy.bis: Ang kusog nga agay sa tubig, sama sa baha, makapalihok sa dagko kaayo ug bug-at nga mga butang, sama sa mga kotse ug kahoy.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Angiosperms are the only plants that produce flowers and fruits
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a physical model or use drawings to demonstrate how the tilt of the Earth relative to its orbit around the Sun affects the intensity of sunlight absorbed by different areas of Earth over a year
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about plant reproduction (angiosperms, flowers, fruits, pollinators). G7-E-10 is about Earth's tilt and sunlight intensity over a year. No connection to Earth/Space content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Angiosperms are the only plants that produce flowers and fruits
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain, using models, how the tilt of the Earth affects the changes in the length of daytime at different times of the year
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses flowers and fruits, not Earth's tilt or daytime length. G7-E-11 is unrelated to plant biology.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Angiosperms are the only plants that produce flowers and fruits
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: G6-E-8 requires a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to explain seasons, star patterns, and eclipses. The card is about angiosperm reproduction, not astronomy.

copy.en: Angiosperms are the only plants that produce flowers and fruits, which help them attract pollinators and protect their seeds.
copy.tl: Ang mga angiosperm lang ang gumagawa ng mga bulaklak at prutas, na tumutulong sa kanila na makaakit ng mga pollinator at maprotektahan ang kanilang mga buto.
copy.bis: Ang mga angiosperm lamang ang naghimo ug mga bulak ug prutas, nga makatabang kanila sa pagdani sa mga pollinator ug pagpanalipod sa ilang mga liso.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fluorescent lamps use ultraviolet radiation to excite a coating inside the tube, which then emits visible light.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how a fluorescent lamp produces visible light via ultraviolet excitation of a coating. It does not address heat energy's role in change of state processes (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fluorescent lamps use ultraviolet radiation to excite a coating inside the tube, which then emits visible light.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the changes of state in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes: a. solid → liquid → vapor, and b. vapor → liquid → solid
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about light emission from a fluorescent lamp, not about changes of state explained by particle arrangement and energy changes (solid-liquid-vapor transitions).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fluorescent lamps use ultraviolet radiation to excite a coating inside the tube, which then emits visible light.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases using diagrams or flowcharts; it concerns ultraviolet radiation and visible light emission.

copy.en: Fluorescent lamps use ultraviolet radiation to excite a coating inside the tube, which then emits visible light.
copy.tl: Ang mga fluorescent lamps ay gumagamit ng ultraviolet radiation para ma-excite ang coating sa loob ng tube, na naglalabas ng visible light.
copy.bis: Ang mga fluorescent lamps mogamit ug ultraviolet radiation aron ma-excite ang coating sa sulod sa tube, nga nagpagawas ug visible light.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A foam is a colloid formed when many gas particles are trapped in a liquid or solid
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches about foam colloids (a chemistry/matter topic). G4-L-5 requires using flow charts to compare animal life-cycle stages (butterfly, frog, chicken, human). There is no life-cycle content or flow-chart format, and the subject is entirely unrelated.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A foam is a colloid formed when many gas particles are trapped in a liquid or solid
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes foam as a colloid, which is a matter/mixtures concept. G5-L-6 requires comparing life cycles of mammals, birds, and plants. No life-cycle content is present, and the topic is unrelated to living things.

copy.en: A foam is a colloid formed when many gas particles are trapped in a liquid or solid, like whipped cream or bubbles.
copy.tl: Ang foam ay isang colloid na nabubuo kapag maraming gas particles ang nakulong sa isang liquid o solid, tulad ng whipped cream o mga bula.
copy.bis: Ang foam usa ka colloid nga maporma kung daghang gas particles ang natanggong sa usa ka liquid o solid, sama sa whipped cream o mga bula.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The focal point is where reflected light rays meet, and the focal length is the distance from the focal point to the vertex
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate various techniques in separating mixtures, such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, and using magnets
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches the optical concepts of focal point and focal length for mirrors. G6-M-6 requires demonstrating mixture separation techniques such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, and using magnets. There is no connection between mirror optics and mixture separation; the card is entirely unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: The focal point is where reflected light rays meet, and the focal length is the distance from the focal point to the vertex, the point where the principal axis meets the mirror.
copy.tl: Ang focal point ay kung saan nagtatagpo ang reflected light rays, at ang focal length ay ang distansya mula sa focal point hanggang sa vertex, ang punto kung saan ang principal axis ay tumatama sa salamin.
copy.bis: Ang focal point mao ang diin magtagbo ang reflected light rays, ug ang focal length mao ang distansya gikan sa focal point ngadto sa vertex, ang punto diin ang principal axis motugpa sa samin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Folds, faults, and thrusts are geological structures that form in response to the stresses and strains generated by plate motion
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes geological structures formed by plate motion, which is Earth science content. G5-F-4 requires identifying gravity as a non-contact force affecting materials and objects. The card provides no information about gravity or non-contact forces, so it does not support the competency.

copy.en: Folds, faults, and thrusts are geological structures that form in response to the stresses and strains generated by plate motion, providing evidence of past tectonic activity.
copy.tl: Ang folds, faults, at thrusts ay mga geological structures na nabubuo bilang tugon sa stresses at strains na dulot ng plate motion, na nagbibigay ng ebidensya ng nakaraang tectonic activity.
copy.bis: Ang folds, faults, ug thrusts kay mga geological structures nga maporma isip tubag sa stresses ug strains nga gipahinabo sa plate motion, nga naghatag ug ebidensya sa kaniadto nga tectonic activity.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Follow evacuation orders from authorities during a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card instructs following evacuation orders during a volcanic eruption, which is a volcanic hazard response. G4-E-4 is about identifying basic weather characteristics (air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, etc.). The card does not support any part of that competency; it is unrelated to weather description.

copy.en: Follow evacuation orders from authorities during a volcanic eruption and stay in the evacuation center until further instructions.
copy.tl: Sundin ang mga utos ng paglikas mula sa mga awtoridad tuwing pumuputok ang bulkan at manatili sa evacuation center hanggang may karagdagang panuto.
copy.bis: Sunda ang mga mando sa pagbakwit gikan sa mga awtoridad kon moubo ang bulkan ug pabilin sa evacuation center hangtod adunay dugang nga instruksyon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Viviparous embryos receive nourishment from the mother through a placenta
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how different factors affect the solubility of a solute in a given solvent, such as heat
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses embryonic nourishment via the placenta, which is biology content. It provides no information about factors affecting solubility of a solute in a solvent, such as heat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Viviparous embryos receive nourishment from the mother through a placenta
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about viviparous embryo nourishment, not about uniform and non-uniform mixtures such as solutions and suspensions.

copy.en: Viviparous embryos receive nourishment from the mother through a placenta, which is why the mother's health is important.
copy.tl: Ang mga embryo ng viviparous na hayop ay kumukuha ng pagkain mula sa ina sa pamamagitan ng placenta, kaya mahalaga ang kalusugan ng ina.
copy.bis: Ang mga embryo sa viviparous nga mananap makakuha ug pagkaon gikan sa inahan pinaagi sa placenta, mao nga importante ang panglawas sa inahan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The magnetic force is related to magnetic field lines
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses magnetic force and field lines, which is physics/magnetism content. G6-M-4 is about uniform and non-uniform mixtures (solutions and suspensions), a chemistry topic. No instructional support for mixtures.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The magnetic force is related to magnetic field lines
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses magnetic force and field lines, which is physics/magnetism content. G7-M-8 is about the role of solute and solvent in a solution, a chemistry topic. No instructional support for solutions.

copy.en: The magnetic force is related to magnetic field lines, because the force is stronger where the field lines are closer together.
copy.tl: Ang magnetic force ay may kaugnayan sa magnetic field lines, dahil mas malakas ang puwersa kung saan mas magkakalapit ang mga field lines.
copy.bis: Ang magnetic force adunay kalambigitan sa magnetic field lines, tungod kay mas kusog ang puwersa diin mas nagkaduol ang mga field lines.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Force can change the size of objects, like cutting wood into smaller pieces or pounding garlic into a paste.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe using labeled diagrams the biotic and abiotic features of tropical rainforests, swamps, estuaries, mangrove forests, and coral reefs
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about force changing the size of objects (a physics/forces concept). G9-L-9 requires describing biotic and abiotic features of specific Philippine ecosystems using labeled diagrams. There is no connection to ecosystems, biodiversity, or labeled diagrams.

copy.en: Force can change the size of objects, like cutting wood into smaller pieces or pounding garlic into a paste.
copy.tl: Ang force ay maaaring magbago ng laki ng mga bagay, tulad ng pag-cut ng kahoy sa maliliit na piraso o pagpukpok ng bawang para maging paste.
copy.bis: Ang force makausab sa gidak-on sa mga butang, sama sa pag-cut sa kahoy ngadto sa gagmay nga mga piraso o pagpukpok sa ahos aron mahimong paste.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A force is a push or pull, and it is a vector quantity
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: construct and annotate distance-time graphs and velocity-time graphs to represent uniform and non-uniform acceleration
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes force as a vector quantity with magnitude and direction. G8-F-3 requires constructing and annotating distance-time and velocity-time graphs for uniform and non-uniform acceleration. The card contains no graph content, acceleration, or velocity-time information, so it does not support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A force is a push or pull, and it is a vector quantity
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe uniform velocity and represent it using distance-time graphs
assignedReviews.reason: G7-F-7 requires describing uniform velocity and representing it using distance-time graphs. The card only defines force as a vector; it does not mention velocity, uniform motion, or distance-time graphs. It is unrelated to the specific competency.

copy.en: A force is a push or pull, and it is a vector quantity, which means it always has both a magnitude (how strong it is) and a direction.
copy.tl: Ang force ay isang tulak o hila, at ito ay isang vector quantity, ibig sabihin laging mayroon itong magnitude (kung gaano kalakas) at direksyon.
copy.bis: Ang force mao ang pagtulod o pagbira, ug kini usa ka vector quantity, nagpasabot nga kanunay kini adunay magnitude (unsa ka kusog) ug direksyon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Electrostatic force can act on an uncharged body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains electrostatic force on uncharged bodies, which is unrelated to the competency 'explain the difference between heat and temperature'. No heat or temperature content is present.

copy.en: Electrostatic force can act on an uncharged body, meaning an object with a balance of charge, not just on other charged bodies.
copy.tl: Ang electrostatic force ay maaaring kumilos sa uncharged body, ibig sabihin isang bagay na may balanseng charge, hindi lamang sa iba pang charged body.
copy.bis: Ang electrostatic force mahimong molihok sa uncharged body, nagpasabot usa ka butang nga adunay balanse nga charge, dili lamang sa laing charged body.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When you squeeze a soft rubber ball or stretch a rubber band, the force changes the object's shape and size.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how forces change the shape of objects, a physics/forces concept. G8-M-4 is about properties of pure substances (fixed chemical composition, unique protons), which is unrelated to force-induced shape changes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When you squeeze a soft rubber ball or stretch a rubber band, the force changes the object's shape and size.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about forces changing shape, not about uniform and non-uniform mixtures such as solutions and suspensions. No instructional support for G6-M-4.

copy.en: When you squeeze a soft rubber ball or stretch a rubber band, the force changes the object's shape and size.
copy.tl: Kapag pinisil mo ang malambot na rubber ball o iniunat ang rubber band, binabago ng force ang hugis at sukat ng bagay.
copy.bis: Kung imong pisliton ang humok nga rubber ball o ibton ang rubber band, usbon sa force ang porma ug gidak-on sa butang.
